title: Container queries
learningObjectives: Explain container queries and apply it to responsive components.

understand.concept: Container queries allow a component to adapt based on the size or state of an ancestor query container. Declare a container with container-type or container shorthand, then use @container to apply styles when its conditions match.
understand.whyItMatters: Reusable components may be placed in sidebars, cards, or main content regions on the same viewport. Container queries let the component respond to its own available space.
understand.analogy: A viewport query asks about the whole room; a container query asks about the particular workspace where the component is placed.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; media and container queries use formal CSS conditions and sizing references.

explain.narrative: The card changes from stacked to two-column layout when its query container reaches the threshold.

practise.guidedTask: Place the same component in two containers of different widths and use @container to adapt the layout.
practise.independentTask: Build a reusable component and test it at different viewport and container sizes, with long labels and text enlargement.
hints: Inspect the actual query condition and container.
Test just below and above thresholds.
Keep content and keyboard order logical.

questions.prompt: What must be declared before an ancestor can be queried as a size container?
options: A query container using container-type or container
questions.answer: A query container using container-type or container
questions.explanation: Container queries evaluate conditions against an ancestor that establishes a query container.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable responsive test?
options: Test different widths and content lengths
Test only at one standard phone size
questions.answer: Test different widths and content lengths
questions.explanation: Responsive behaviour depends on actual space and content, not just a device label.
